region.name: VP Engineering Hire & Pods
region.summary: Covers the post-Series B plan to hire a VP Engineering and 12 engineers into restructured pods, including the VPE profile, interview loop, screening criteria, tech lead expectations, hiring sequencing, and associated risks.

brief.text:
This region covers Stencil's post-Series B engineering expansion. The hiring plan was approved at Eng Staff. It adds 12 engineering hires plus a VP Engineering over the 9 months after the Series B close, which is roughly 40% growth on a base of 31 engineers. It targets fragile, high bus-factor areas: money movement, mobile, security/compliance (including SOC 2 Type II), and ops. The 12 roles are backend payments, iOS, Android, data/ML, SRE, security, growth, and one engineering manager. The VP Engineering search runs separately. The structural motivation is that the current engineering leader is a bottleneck: they sit in every 1:1, every architecture decision, the hiring loop, and onboarding. Their weekly 1:1s include Aleks Varga, the tech leads, Lin Zhao, Renee Alvarez, and direct-report ICs, plus a monthly engineering all-hands. The proposed structure is about 25 engineers in 3-4 pods, with a VPE between the leader and the tech leads instead of multiple line managers. The pods are Money Movement (Payments & Platform), Mobile, Growth + Data, and a new Infra + Platform pod that needs a tech lead hire.

The VPE profile asks for someone from a Series A/B fintech with an IC background who has led 10-30 engineers, is strong at hiring, and communicates directly. The disposition criteria are direct communicator, comfortable with ambiguity, strong opinions loosely held, and genuine care for engineers. The ambiguity point is an open todo: Stencil's environment is choppy with Series B in flight. The anti-patterns to screen out are process maximalist, manager-only career, conflict-avoidant, and status player. Process maximalist, meaning someone who solves every problem with more meetings and frameworks, is tracked as the highest-severity open risk (70). The interview loop has five rounds, takes about 8 hours over 2-3 weeks, and has no coding interview. The rounds are a CTO screen, a founder-fit conversation with Aleks Varga, a tech lead panel that holds veto power, a live case study, and offline reference deep-dives.

Sequencing depends on three prerequisites: a higher offer-accept rate, more trained interviewers, and onboarding that no longer depends on Marcus. The other open risks are lower severity. They include the offer-accept rate and the senior iOS compensation band (28), adding 12 hires with no EM layer (4, owned by Maya), and the Series B close slipping so that Q4 hires push into Q1 (4). Typical questions this region answers include which roles are being hired and for which pod, who sits on the VPE interview loop and who holds veto, what traits disqualify a VPE candidate, why the plan chose a VPE over line managers, how hiring is staged against the close, and which risks are open and who owns them.
